bays.title: Keyboard
bays.say: Play a sine synthesizer from the on-screen keys or a MIDI keyboard plugged into this computer.

bays.title: Recorder
bays.say: Record what you play and play it back, every note in a table with its time, velocity and length.

bays.title: Timeline
bays.say: The same recorder drawn on a timeline, so a take shows as notes in time and plays from its start.

bays.title: Sound design
bays.say: One voice from the keys through a filter, an envelope and an LFO, every knob on a wire of its own.

bays.title: Faust synth
bays.say: A Faust synth voice compiled in this tab on your first key, with a knob for each of its parameters.

bays.title: Collide synth
bays.say: Play a small SuperCollider program from the keys and edit its code, recompiled when you stop typing.

bays.title: Sound wish
bays.say: Type or say a wish for a sound and a model writes it in SuperCollider. Play it from the keys.

bays.title: Plaits
bays.say: The same Plaits voice played from the keys or a MIDI keyboard, with all ten controls as knobs.

bays.title: Piano and Rhodes
bays.say: A grand piano and a Rhodes on SuperCollider, looped by the sustain pedal with no tempo and no grid.

bays.title: Dot piano
bays.say: Each note draws an arc on a ring, by a shader in this tab and by C firmware on an emulated Pico.

bays.title: Granulator
bays.say: Our radio recordings granulated in this tab, each grain marked on the wave where it read the sound.

bays.title: Beat granulator
bays.say: The Ida recording granulated on Dub, its echo and grains put on the beat a tempo detector hears.

bays.title: Circuit on Pi
bays.say: A Novation Circuit in another building, played from here through its Pi. Keys, MIDI and 8 macros.

bays.title: Collide on Pi
bays.say: SuperCollider here and on a Pi in another building at once. Crossfade between the two.

bays.title: Piano and Rhodes on Pi
bays.say: A piano and a Rhodes on a Pi in another building, played from here over the relay or direct.

bays.title: Plaits on Pi
bays.say: Emilie Gillet's Plaits running on a Pi in another building. Play it and turn its knobs from here.

bays.title: Blend
bays.say: Listen to Vikerraadio and Ida Radio Tallinn live and blend between them on a crossfader.

bays.title: Tuner
bays.say: Turn one dial across four live stations, as on an old AM set, with noise and a whistle in between.

bays.title: Tempo
bays.say: Find the tempo of recordings of Raadio 2, Raadio 4 and Ida, with the beats it hears on the wave.

bays.title: Live tempo
bays.say: The same tempo detector on Raadio 2, Raadio 4 or Ida live, one station at a time through our relay.

bays.title: Live key
bays.say: Hear a live station, see the key a detector finds in it lit on a keyboard, and play along in it.

bays.title: Radio landscape
bays.say: Live radio, granulated, blends slowly from station to station through tuning noise. The waves rise.

bays.title: Camera
bays.say: Turn on your camera and see it on the page while the patchbay holds the link from camera to screen.

bays.title: Camera shader
bays.say: Your camera beside itself through a two tone dither shader, with one knob for how coarse it is.

bays.title: Camera recorder
bays.say: Record up to ten seconds of your camera and play it back on a timeline, kept in this browser.

bays.title: WebRTC loopback
bays.say: Your camera over WebRTC to Cloudflare Stream and back beside the original, with the delay timed.

bays.title: LL-HLS loopback
bays.say: Your camera to Cloudflare Stream and back as LL-HLS beside the original, with the delay timed.

bays.title: MoQ loopback
bays.say: Your camera over MoQ to Cloudflare's relay and back beside the original, with the delay timed.

bays.title: Mirror shader
bays.say: A kaleidoscope shader with one knob for its mirrors, and code that recompiles as you edit.

bays.title: Scan landscape
bays.say: A radio recording drawn as a scan landscape. Six knobs shape the ridges.

bays.title: Shader on Pi
bays.say: A kaleidoscope shader here and on a Pi in another building, each change timed to its first frame.

bays.title: Picture wish
bays.say: Type or say a wish for a picture and a model writes its shader. The code stays in the box to edit.

bays.title: Chat
bays.say: A chat window whose every line crosses the room along a patchbay link, drawn underneath.

bays.title: Broadcast chat
bays.say: Whoever joins first is admin and broadcasts in a column of their own while the rest chat beside.

bays.title: Chat timeline
bays.say: The broadcast chat with a memory: until you join, the room's last fifty lines replay at their pace.

bays.title: Paper
bays.say: A sheet of white paper to type on, with a blocky cursor and a page that opens full screen.

bays.title: Typewriter
bays.say: The same paper, now sounding like a Hermes Precisa 305 typewriter, bell and all.

bays.title: Typewriters
bays.say: The typewriter through an effects box where every number gives a different machine.

bays.title: Playback
bays.say: Everything you type, deletions included, is kept and played back as the page writes itself again.

bays.title: Multi typer
bays.say: Up to six papers typed at once from a written score, each through a typewriter of its own.

bays.title: Drum machine
bays.say: Four SuperCollider drums on 16 steps, each on a patchbay wire that silences it when taken away.

bays.title: Drum knobs
bays.say: The same drum machine with a knob and a waveform for each drum, heard from the next hit.

bays.title: Sample drums
bays.say: Drop a Circuit pack or WAVs and each sample becomes a named row. Drag across the grid to draw hits.

bays.title: Camera drums
bays.say: Point your camera and its picture plays as a 16 by 9 drum pattern, where brighter areas play busier.

bays.title: Drums on the Pi
bays.say: One drum pattern here and on a Pi in another building at the same moment. Crossfade the two.

bays.title: Newsreels
bays.say: ERR's 1965 newsreels on a line, each silent film played with that day's surviving radio.
